instantiated_cells.justification: Principals must file expense statements on or before July 31 and January 31 (semiannual), not annually.
The statute requires filing by July 31 and January 31 for each reporting period, not monthly.
Reporting is specified as twice yearly (July 31 and January 31), so no other frequency option applies.
Principals file twice per year (covering each 6-month reporting period), not quarterly.
Expense statements are due on or before July 31 and January 31 and cover a 'reporting period' defined as a 6-month period, i.e., semi-annual reporting.
The required reporting periods are fixed 6-month periods (Jan-Jun; Jul-Dec), not tri-annual or linked to a legislative calendar.
Registration requires a description of the principal's business activity (or nature and purposes) depending on principal type, disclosing the nature of the business/organization.
The expense statement must include aggregate lobbying expenditures including 'compensation to lobbyists for lobbying' and reimbursements.
The report requires daily itemization of time spent meeting/research but does not require disclosure of the identities of contacts communicated with.
Principals must report each legislative proposal/budget bill subject/rule number or, if none, each topic of lobbying communications, and must estimate time by topic accounting for 10% or more.
Principals must report reimbursements paid to officials for actual and reasonable expenses authorized under §13.621(7)(a), which are travel/living-type costs.
The statement must include office overhead costs (office space, utilities, supplies, compensation of employees used in preparing lobbying) and total personal travel and living expenses.
When payments to a lobbyist exceed $200, the principal lists the lobbyist's name and address, but the statute does not require the lobbyist's phone number.
The expense statement lists a lobbyist only if payments to that lobbyist exceed $200 during the reporting period, so not all lobbyists are always required to be disclosed in the spending report.
Neither the expense statement nor the registration statement requires disclosure of major financial contributors to the principal.
The registration statement must include the principal's name and business address, but the statute does not require the principal's telephone number.
Principals must report each legislative proposal and proposed administrative rule number in connection with which they made or intend to make a lobbying communication.
The expense statement must report the aggregate total amount of lobbying expenditures made and obligations incurred for lobbying by the principal and all lobbyists for the principal.
The law requires reporting compensation to lobbyists for lobbying and, if payments to a lobbyist exceed $200, listing the lobbyist with the total amount paid/obligated.
Expenditures are reported primarily as aggregate totals (with limited listing of lobbyists over $200), rather than a fully itemized transaction-by-transaction spending report.
Associations must report approximate number of members and CEO, but there is no requirement to list names of all sponsors or members.

If payments to any lobbyist exceed $200 during the reporting period, the expense statement must list the lobbyist's name and address, effectively requiring listing employed lobbyists above the threshold.
